newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends down at post-crisis low.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends down at post-crisis low.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate plummeted 110 basis points to close at 19.00 percent on Thursday, its lowest level since the financial crisis triggered by an abrupt devaluation of the peso in December 1994.
Traders said the fall was due to a big player flooding the market with liquidity at the close.
Overnight Cetes rates had traded for most of the session at 19.90 percent.
"It was a quiet day. Market rates were between 19.80-20.00 percent and we stayed there for a while as the peso was firm," a trader said.

"Nonetheless, a big player threw money at the market towards the close and that brought rates down further. We thus expect the market to return to today's average rates when it opens tomorrow," he added.
Other traders said the market was discounting future falls in inflation.
"The market is buying ahead of lower inflation, and as the peso is stable, there is nothing else to put pressure on rates," one trader said. "Some even feel rates may continue to decline."
Dealers said lower U.S. interest rates also helped secondary Cetes rates to fall.
Yields on U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds declined to 6.63 percent, down from 6.72 percent on Wednesday.
Overnight rates on bank paper closed down 70 basis points at 21.00 percent.
Banco de Mexico offset surplus liquidity in the market by draining 524 million pesos through two auctions.
Liquidity of 1.639 billion pesos was expected to return to the system on Friday from prior central bank participation.
